evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: 'Runs use shared capacity, so you don't reserve GPUs before you start.'
Setting scope='serverless' makes creation fail instead of falling back to dedicated mode when serverless cannot take the run.
The default scope can choose dedicated mode for unsupported models, ranks, or sequence lengths.
Capacity saturation can produce HTTP 429; the SDK attempts a creation request up to ten times before LoopsCapacityError.
'baseten loops usage' reports dedicated GPU allocations; it does not report serverless token usage or spend.

Serverless bills separately for prefill, cached prefill, sample, and train tokens; idle time between operations does not bill. Saved checkpoints remain available to download, deploy, or start a new run.
inspection_records.relevance: Establishes shared-service confounds, mandatory explicit serverless scope, and why a zero-GPU CLI readout is neither a hardware disclosure nor an invoice.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

inspection_records.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Abstract, Section 4.1-4.2; inspected low-rank update equation, initialization, scaling, and target-module discussion.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: The pretrained matrix remains frozen while the forward function uses W0 + BA; A is initialized randomly and B at zero. The update is scaled by alpha/r.
inspection_records.relevance: Frozen base weights do not imply an unchanged adapted function. Rank, alpha, target modules, initialization, and the adapter-disabled baseline belong in the manifest.

inspection_records.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full PDF; inspected abstract, introduction, low-rank parameterization, and adaptation objective.
inspection_records.evidence: LoRA freezes pretrained weights and trains low-rank update matrices. Published quality and resource comparisons are specific to the authors’ tested models and configurations.
inspection_records.relevance: Defines the intervention; does not establish that rank 8 is optimal or that this Baseten experiment has a particular memory, GPU, or throughput advantage.

sources.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment

inspection_records.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Abstract, Sections 2, 3, 5, and 6; inspected data construction, optimizer and checkpoint selection, diversity/quality/quantity ablations, and dialogue extension.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: The paper defines the Superficial Alignment Hypothesis; trains a 65B LLaMA with 1,000 curated examples; and reports improved dialogue behavior after adding 30 dialogue chains. Its 7B diversity experiments acknowledge source confounds, and checkpoint choice used a 50-example development set.
inspection_records.relevance: Small amounts of training can change output style and conditional behavior. This is evidence for testing format and state-distribution changes, not proof that the present regression is merely superficial.

sources.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less

inspection_records.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Abstract, Sections 4.2-4.3 and 4.7, Appendix B.2 and C; inspected forgetting metrics, training-duration effects, learning/forgetting comparisons, and rank/alpha/learning-rate sweeps.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: Across the studied code/math settings, LoRA generally retains more source-domain performance than full finetuning, while forgetting increases with training duration; the paper reports sensitivity to rank, target modules, alpha, and learning rate. Some high-rank math runs forget nearly as much as full finetuning.
inspection_records.relevance: Forgetting is possible under LoRA, but this study does not establish a mechanism for rank-8 Qwen with 96 assistant turns. Its recommended hyperparameters must not be transplanted as validated for this model.

sources.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

inspection_records.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Sections 4.1.1-4.1.2; inspected PPO/GRPO objective, group baseline, outcome reward normalization and per-token advantage assignment.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: Outcome-supervised GRPO assigns each output token the group-normalized reward (reward minus group mean, divided by group standard deviation).
inspection_records.relevance: Equal rewards contain no relative outcome learning signal. The project uses mean-centering without standard-deviation division and the provider cispo loss, so it should be described as a group-relative policy-gradient baseline rather than an exact reproduction of GRPO.

sources.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale

inspection_records.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Sections 3.2-3.4, Algorithm 1, and experiment-setting paragraphs; inspected zero-advantage groups, dynamic sampling, token-level weighting, and generation-budget considerations.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: Section 3.2 explicitly states that equal-reward groups have zero advantage and zero policy gradients; it oversamples and filters all-correct/all-wrong prompts. Section 3.3 contrasts sample-level and token-level loss reduction.
inspection_records.relevance: Zero-variance skipping and dynamic sampling are published ideas. Their compute tradeoffs on large synchronized long-reasoning training do not imply that oversampling is free for token-billed short SQL rollouts.

sources.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning

inspection_records.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Abstract, Section 1 and Section 3 algorithm; inspected learner-induced state distribution and dataset aggregation procedure.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: A learner action can change future observations, invalidating the expert-state i.i.d. assumption. DAgger collects states under the learned policy and aggregates expert labels on those states.
inspection_records.relevance: Expert SQL/tool-result prefixes may fail to cover learner-generated states. This motivates cross-context evaluation or labelled recovery states, but does not prove long-horizon compounding in a two-tool-call task.

inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.

sources.title: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites

inspection_records.title: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites
inspection_records.inspection_method: Retrieved complete primary-source HTML by HTTPS, extracted visible text with Python HTMLParser, then read the listed relevant sections. No search snippets used.
inspection_records.inspection_depth: Abstract, introduction examples, test-suite rationale, and Section 6.4; inspected single-database false positives and finite multi-database execution evaluation.
inspection_records.evidence_excerpt_or_observed_finding: A semantically wrong query may match the gold denotation on a single database. The method distills databases from random candidates using gold-query coverage and compares denotations across the suite; it approximates semantic accuracy, rather than proving arbitrary SQL equivalence.
inspection_records.relevance: The planned eight-perturbation replay is an application of established execution-testing ideas. It is not the published coverage-distillation procedure and not an end-to-end agent counterfactual evaluation.

inspection_records.title: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full 16-page paper; inspected abstract, introduction, suite construction, neighbor-query coverage, and semantic-accuracy rationale.
inspection_records.evidence: Single-database execution can accept semantically wrong SQL. The authors build suites using randomly generated databases and neighbor-query distinctions, then compare predicted and gold denotations. Finite suites approximate semantic correctness.
inspection_records.relevance: Strong primary precedent for replaying SQL on perturbed databases. Eight hand-designed deterministic variants are a diagnostic suite, not a reproduction of the paper’s distillation procedure or a proof of semantic equivalence.

sources.title: Improving Text-to-SQL Evaluation Methodology

inspection_records.title: Improving Text-to-SQL Evaluation Methodology
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full 10-page paper; inspected abstract, introduction, data standardization, query deduplication, and query-based splitting rationale.
inspection_records.evidence: Question-based splits can share SQL structures across train and test after entity substitution. The paper proposes a query-based split and shows a template baseline can appear competitive on conventional splits.
inspection_records.relevance: Primary precedent for separating query generalization from paraphrase robustness. Family-disjoint evaluation must be defined beyond entity or schema renaming.

sources.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing

inspection_records.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full 10-page paper; inspected sections on paired tests, McNemar, paired bootstrap, and dependent observations.
inspection_records.evidence: McNemar is presented for paired binary outcomes; the paper warns that independence assumptions are often violated in language datasets.
inspection_records.relevance: Use the same task IDs across conditions and analyze paired correctness, while retaining dependence induced by repeated templates or tasks.

sources.title: Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers over Multiple Data Sets

inspection_records.title: Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers over Multiple Data Sets
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full 30-page paper; inspected introduction, distinction between datasets and within-dataset samples, and Holm multiple-comparison discussion.
inspection_records.evidence: For comparisons across datasets, sample size refers to independent datasets, not the number of examples within each. The paper describes Holm step-down adjustment and its general use for controlling family-wise error.
inspection_records.relevance: Four templates are not 200 independent samples of SQL families. Multiplicity must include planned family and policy comparisons.

sources.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation

inspection_records.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full 29-page paper; inspected abstract, introduction, model-selection variance and evaluation protocol argument.
inspection_records.evidence: The variance of a finite-sample selection criterion allows overfitting during selection. Evaluation should compare combinations of learning algorithms and selection procedures; selection must occur inside the fitting protocol.
inspection_records.relevance: Checkpoint Gate is a selection policy. Test performance after selecting on the same test is optimistically biased. Ordinary validation selection is established methodology.

sources.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks

inspection_records.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full PDF; inspected abstract, introduction, recommendations, and formal model of data, training, and hyperparameter variability. The PDF also contains a 2020 proceedings footer; this record uses its explicit arXiv version date rather than inferring a venue date.
inspection_records.evidence: Data sampling, parameter initialization, and hyperparameter choices all contribute variance. Varying initialization alone leaves other variation unmeasured.
inspection_records.relevance: Three training seeds are a minimum diagnostic replication, not a universal precision guarantee or an estimate of dataset/family variation.

sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice

inspection_records.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
inspection_records.date: 2021 conference paper; retrieved arXiv v4 dated 2022-01-05
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full PDF including appendix; inspected introduction, evaluation formalism, few-run limitations, and stratified bootstrap recommendations.
inspection_records.evidence: The paper recommends interval estimates and stratified bootstrap instead of point estimates alone. Its examples show that even conventional run counts can leave large uncertainty; it does not establish that three runs are sufficient universally.
inspection_records.relevance: Report every seed and the family-by-seed matrix. Adapt resampling to this experiment’s crossed seed/task structure rather than copying RL software blindly.

sources.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results

inspection_records.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full 10-page paper; inspected abstract, introduction, expected validation performance versus computation budget, and reporting rationale.
inspection_records.evidence: Model comparisons can change as hyperparameter-search budget changes; reporting only the final test score omits consequential selection effort.
inspection_records.relevance: Release training/evaluation/search budgets and all considered checkpoints. Compare Gate with ordinary selection at the same candidate and evaluation budget.

sources.title: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet?

inspection_records.title: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet?
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full paper; inspected abstract, introduction, fresh-test construction rationale, and decomposition into adaptivity, distribution, and sampling gaps.
inspection_records.evidence: Freshly collected test sets produced substantial accuracy drops even when construction closely followed the original process. The authors specifically find adaptivity unlikely to explain their observed drops.
inspection_records.relevance: New tests can change difficulty or distribution. This is precedent for fresh evaluation, not proof that Checkpoint Gate’s existing results are caused by contamination or adaptivity.

sources.title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses

inspection_records.title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved and parsed full-text XML from Europe PMC after the PMC HTML URL returned a challenge page; inspected equivalence, dependent means, power, bounds, and interpretation sections.
inspection_records.evidence: A nonsignificant difference does not support absence of a meaningful effect. Equivalence requires prespecified meaningful bounds and sufficient precision; narrower bounds require larger samples.
inspection_records.relevance: A regression gate cannot claim noninferiority because a harm test fails to reject. Use a justified absolute accuracy margin and an appropriate paired-binary interval, not this paper’s t-test formulas mechanically.

sources.title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences

inspection_records.title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
inspection_records.date: Retrieved arXiv v9 dated 2022-08-06; PDF title page 2022-08-09
inspection_records.inspection: Retrieved full PDF; inspected introduction, uniform-coverage definition, stopping-rule properties, and fixed-time versus time-uniform interval illustration.
inspection_records.evidence: Continuous monitoring with fixed-sample intervals can inflate error. Confidence sequences offer time-uniform coverage under stated assumptions and are generally wider.
inspection_records.relevance: Use a fixed prospective test or a genuinely prespecified sequential method. Optional stopping over task clusters and training seeds requires the right statistical units.
